Decorative line | `alt=""` — leave the alt attribute empty | 0 | ## Example HTML ```html ``` ```html ``` For the decorative line, use an empty `alt` if it is an image: ```html ``` Even better, if the line is purely visual, make it with CSS instead of an image, so no alt text is needed at all. ## How long should alt text be? There is no strict legal character limit, but a good practical rule is: - **Aim for under 125 characters** for most images. - **Under 100 characters is often ideal** for simple images. - **For charts or complex graphics**, use a short alt text that gives the key information, and add a longer description or data table nearby if the exact details matter. So for your chart, the alt text above is a good length. If the exact numbers are very important, also include a small accessible table next to the chart, like this: ```html
Club participants per year
Year Participants
202114
202222
202331
202429
``` A few extra tips: - You usually do **not** need to write “photo of” or “image of” unless the fact that it is a photo is important. - For decorative images, use `alt=""`, not no `alt` attribute. - If the surrounding page text already explains the photo, the alt text can be shorter. For example, if the page already says the trip was to Belchenflue, you could use: ```html alt="Nine hikers in rain jackets on a foggy ridge." ```
